name: Marshlands
summary: The Tanaris trail brings travelers into Un'Goro through the Marshlands. Raptors hunt among the wetlands, where Blue Power Crystals lie scattered and two wilderness experts keep apart.

sections.title: Gateway to the Crater
sections.body: From Tanaris, the trail descends into the Marshlands. It is the only safe way down Un'Goro's sheer crater rim. Dense canopies, standing water, and mud conceal packs of fierce raptors. Some are venomous hunters that stalk the reeds. Blue Power Crystals, found nowhere else in Un'Goro, lie across damp clearings.

sections.title: Encampments in the Bog
sections.body: Several wilderness experts keep solitary outposts in the dangerous marsh. Torwa Pathfinder, a tauren hunter, watches the primeval fauna from a prominent earthen mound. Across the wetlands, Mor'vek studies and trains native ravasaurs. Mor'vek is a troll.

faq.q: Why is the Marshlands usually the first area people see in Un'Goro?
faq.answer: Un'Goro's sheer crater cliffs make any approach beyond the southeastern pass from Tanaris almost certainly fatal. The descending ramp leads into the Marshlands, so travelers on foot pass through its wetlands.

faq.q: What creatures are most common here?
faq.answer: Raptors fill the Marshlands, from ordinary hunters to venomous kinds that stalk the thick brush.

faq.q: What unique resources are found in the Marshlands?
faq.answer: Blue Power Crystals form naturally only in the Marshlands. Researchers prize them for studying the mysterious crystalline pylons scattered through the basin.
Torwa Pathfinder is a tauren hunter who watches Un'Goro's fauna from a prominent mound in the Marshlands.

faq.q: Can the ravasaurs here be tamed or trained?
faq.answer: Yes. Mor'vek is a troll based across the wetlands who studies and trains native ravasaurs.

angles.text: As a hunter, you can test your wilderness skills against swift raptors, venomous predators, and rare beasts. Torwa Pathfinder watches the local fauna.
As a herbalist, you can find aggressive bloodpetal saplings and damp foliage along the marsh's northern edges. The plants here are hostile and mobile.
